figures.finding: The Civil Code of 1977 sets the age of majority at 18 solar years, from which a person has full legal capacity in transactions; whether the present de facto authorities apply it is not shown by any source reached.
figures.applies: Civil Code 1977 art. 39, in the English text reproduced by Yale Law School's Reproductive Rights site (edited September 2005); the Ministry of Justice's and ACKU's own copies were not reached (ACKU bot-checks this client). Its application since 2021 is not modeled.
figures.webSearch: 2026-11-01: 'Afghanistan Civil Code age of majority 18 years article' returned the Yale reproduction (used), ACKU's law.acku.edu.af/?p=9740 (Civil Code entry; Cloudflare bot check, not read), worldlawdigest; 'قانون مدنی افغانستان ماده ۳۹ سن رشد هجده سال شمسی' returned only Iranian Civil Code pages.

sources.said: The age of majority is 18 solar years. Person attaining majority age shall be recognized as having full legal personality in business transactions.

figures.finding: The Labour Law (2007) art. 13 bars employing anyone under 18, lets a 15-year-old work in light industries for at most 35 hours a week (s. 31, ages 15 to 18) and takes trainees from 14; on ratifying ILO Convention 138 Afghanistan declared 14 as its minimum age. Whether the present de facto authorities apply the law is not shown.
figures.applies: Labour Law 2007 (Presidential Decree No. 94) arts. 13, 31, 121-122, as the ILO's child-labour country profile states them; the NATLEX copy of the Law itself answered a Cloudflare block to this client and was not read.
figures.webSearch: 2026-11-01: 'Afghanistan Labour Law 2007 article 13 minimum age employment 18 years 15 years light work' returned the ILO profile (used), Refworld's Labour Law 2007 copy (its UNHCR web archive answered a MirrorWeb browser check; not read), EUAA country guidance, Jurist/HRW. 'قانون کار افغانستان ماده سیزدهم سن استخدام ۱۸ سال ۱۵ سال' returned WageIndicator's Dari pages (minimum employment age 18 under art. 13; 'young employee' 14 to 18), Rivermate, Afghanistan International; no primary text.

sources.said: In ratifying C138, Afghanistan specified a minimum age of 14 years for admission to employment or work within its territory. According to section 13 of the Labour Law, no person under the age of 18 years shall be employed while a child of 15 years may be employed in light industries, and for trainees, the minimum age is 14 years. ... Section 13(2) of the Labour Law sets 15 years as the minimum age for employment in light work in industries and section 31 prescribes a weekly working period of 35 hours for young persons between 15 and 18 years.

figures.finding: Under the Civil Code of 1977 a person who, being a minor, does not understand the nature of transactions can perform none, and anyone under seven is deemed so; full capacity comes at 18; the judge is guardian of those who have none. How a minor of seven to eighteen is bound to a contract for work, and any set-aside of earnings, was not found.
figures.applies: Civil Code 1977 arts. 39, 40, 78 in Yale Law School's reproduction; partial: the rule for minors of 7 to 18 stays a blocker.

sources.said: Person who does not understand the nature of transactions due to minority of age, mental retardation or insanity, cannot perform any legal transactions. Person not attaining the age of seven years shall be deemed as a person not understanding the nature of transactions. ... The judge is the guardian of persons having no guardians.

figures.finding: The Law of Commerce (1334) lets everyone who has reached eighteen and is not legally barred carry on commercial activity; a business that passes to a minor goes on only through a legal agent where the authorities find it in the minor's interest. The Corporations and LLC Law's own founder rule was not reached.

value.minorsBusiness: through legal agent, if authorities find it beneficial

figures.applies: Law of Commerce 1334 (1955), English text in WIPO Lex (AF005); whether the present de facto authorities apply it is not shown.
figures.webSearch: 2026-11-01: 'Afghanistan Law on Corporations and Limited Liability Companies founder shareholder age legal capacity 18' returned WIPO Lex's Law of Commerce (used), Moore's draft Company Law, incorporations.io's Corporations and LLC Law text (purpose and definitions only in the snippet), trade guides.

sources.said: Article 4. Every individual having reached the age of eighteen is permitted to engage in commercial activities provided he is not legally debarred of his legal rights. Article 5. When a business has passed to a minor, the legal authorities shall consider if the continuation of such a trade by his legal agent is beneficial to the interest of the minor.
